operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 1 revokes Executive Order 6964 of February 5, 1935, as amended, as to one 20-acre tract in Arkansas. It is a one-time act that took effect when the order issued: the order states no later effective date, it is signed 1938-08-12 and was filed with the Federal Register on 1938-08-13. The command was therefore performed and exhausted on 1938-08-12, and that date is recorded as its first end with the order's own text as the source. A later revocation of an order does not prove the first cessation of a command already performed, so Public Land Order 3277 is recorded as a later event rather than as this clause's end: its paragraph 4 states the intent to re-embrace the lands in the Executive Order 6964 withdrawal immediately upon the date of that order, 1963-12-03, which reverses the surviving effect of section 1. If a reviewer treats the removal of the tract from the Executive Order 6964 withdrawal as lasting until then, this clause's end date moves to 1963-12-03 and the whole-order end date is unchanged.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 2 temporarily withdraws the 20-acre tract from settlement, location, sale or entry, subject to valid existing rights, and reserves it for use by the State of Arkansas as a forest-fire lookout tower site. It is a continuing reservation. Public Land Order 3277, headed Revoking Executive Order No. 7951 of August 12, 1938 and dated 1963-12-03, revokes the order for exactly this tract. The revocation operates on the date of the public land order (paragraph 4 speaks of re-embracing the lands in the Executive Order 6964 withdrawal immediately upon that date); the restoration of the land to the public land laws at 10:00 a.m. on 1964-01-08 in paragraph 2 is the opening of the land to entry, a consequence of the revocation, and is not the end of the reservation. The alternative reading, that the reservation lasted through 1964-01-08, is recorded here for the reviewer. The public land order was published in the Federal Register of 1963-12-07 at 28 FR 13306.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section 3 provides that section 2 continues in force until revoked by the President or by act of Congress. It sets no calendar date; it makes revocation the event that ends section 2, so it has no content of its own after section 2 ends. The event occurred on 1963-12-03 when Public Land Order 3277 revoked the order. That public land order was signed by the Assistant Secretary of the Interior under authority vested in the President by section 1 of the act of June 25, 1910 and Executive Order 10355 of May 26, 1952, both stated in its lead-in; Executive Order 10355 is not held in this packet, so the delegation is relied on as stated on the face of the public land order. This clause ends on the same date as section 2.

Doc. 38-2371, filed 1938-08-13. The order has three numbered sections: section 1 revokes Executive Order 6964 as to one 20-acre tract; section 2 temporarily withdraws and reserves that tract for a State of Arkansas forest-fire lookout tower; section 3 says section 2 continues in force until revoked by the President or by act of Congress. The dossier inventory (sec1, sec2, sec3) is complete; the recital paragraph is not a command. Doc. 63-12673, filed 1963-12-06). The public land order revokes the whole order for the whole tract, restores the land to the public land laws effective 1964-01-08 subject to valid existing rights, and puts the tract back inside the earlier Executive Order 6964 withdrawal, which is an independent instrument with its own lifecycle and is not a command of this order. The order's own reservation was also made subject to valid existing rights, so the public land order creates no new savings. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Paragraph 1 orders that the tract of about 9,300 acres within the described Turnagain Arm boundaries be excluded from the Chugach National Forest. It is a one-time act that took effect when the order issued; the order states no later effective date and is dated 1940-07-12 (filed 1940-07-13). The command was performed and exhausted on 1940-07-12, recorded as its first end with the order's own text as the source. Its consequence, that the tract stays outside the national forest, was not undone by the later revocation: Public Land Order 835, paragraph 1, revokes the order with a proviso that the revocation does not have the effect of returning any of the lands to national forest status. That public land order is therefore recorded as a later event preserving the consequence, not as the end of this clause.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (5 FR 2557, issue of 1940-07-16, fr-originals) prints the number No. 8480 and the date July 12, 1940 after the order and is headed Excluding Certain Land From the Chugach National Forest and Reserving it for Townsite Purposes (Alaska). The held text is a reading-order extract in which the order's body is interrupted by the issue's contents column, masthead and the first lines of an unrelated Department of Agriculture marketing order, and its signature block is printed after that marketing text. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory (15 clauses starting at character 3279 and running to 12012) is not the order; it takes page furniture and the marketing order for clauses. The order has two operative paragraphs: (1) the tract of about 9,300 acres lying within the described Turnagain Arm boundaries is excluded from the Chugach National Forest, under the act of June 4, 1897; (2) under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305, 307) the same tract is withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry or other disposition and reserved for townsite purposes in connection with the construction and operation of railroad lines. I replaced the inventory with two exact spans of the held text: characters 3279 to 9328 (paragraph 1, which includes the page furniture that falls inside the boundary description) and 9329 to 9781 (paragraph 2). The numeral 9,300 acres closes the first span. Ending: Public Land Order 835 (17 FR 4948, held page extract jobs/selden-fr-acting/output/texts/FR_17_4948.txt, sha256 7d4ce09b9fbae911cb373617d34b55faf1822e143bce9b331be66ee80faa8077, bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-835-EO-8480) is headed Revocation of Executive Order No. 8480 of July 12, 1940 and its paragraph 1 revokes the order, with a proviso that the revocation does not return any of the lands to national forest status; it is signed by the Secretary of the Interior on May 23, 1952 (F.R. Doc. 52-5945, filed 1952-05-29). Earlier partial events: Public Land Order 571 (14 FR 1175, held page extract FR_14_1175.txt, sha256 2cff211ecf5ccd6926fe8639dbb569489f6bda025e32a7cd71927912502d0a6e; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-571-EO-8480) set two parcels aside for The Alaska Railroad and modified the order to the extent necessary; Public Land Order 686 (15 FR 7799, held page extract FR_15_7799.txt, sha256 ab0a69c8d7d98b4eea38e06b49f6d48a977c2e1fac1f14672a9b3a9f1ac8db34; bound as SUPPLEMENT:acting-PLO-686-EO-8480) revoked the order only as to Tract No. 1 (Portage air-navigation site). Selden leads: used the three Federal Register page leads (PLO 571, 686, 835), each read in full; used the statute lead 30 Stat. 11 only as the authority the order itself cites for paragraph 1 (the act of June 4, 1897, 30 Stat. 11, 36; the Act's text was not read for this claim); rejected the statute leads 49 Stat. 115, 49 Stat. 500, 49 Stat. 750, 50 Stat. 246 and 50 Stat. 522, which are artifacts of the neighbouring orders and Federal Register furniture on the same pages; read 38 Stat. 305 (the Alaska Railroad act, authority for paragraph 2) and found nothing ending a withdrawal before 1952.
